**Paper Engines: The Age of Mechanical Calculators**
*May 10 – October 4, 2026*

Before silicon, there were gears, levers, and brass. *Paper Engines* traces the remarkable century when inventors taught machines to count, and in doing so reshaped commerce, science, and everyday work.

Eighty-five calculating machines fill the galleries, from elegant desktop curiosities to the rugged workhorses of banks, railways, and observatories. At the heart of the exhibition stands an 1851 arithmometer, among the earliest calculators to be produced commercially and trusted by clerks and engineers across Europe. Its stepped drum mechanism, still crisp after more than 170 years, reveals the ingenuity packed inside a polished wooden case.

Turn a crank, read the results, and discover how these machines worked, who built them, and why their makers believed arithmetic could be automated. Together, they tell the story of a world learning to compute, one rotation at a time.

*(About 150 words)*
